That threshold is not met here because the content does not market food at all. The entire sponsorship message is about grooming tools and body-care items: trimmers, deodorant, toner spray, and related accessories. Those are personal-care products, not edible products.

The content is clearly commercial, because it identifies a sponsor, describes product features, and gives a discount code and purchase prompt. But that only shows it is an advertisement. It does not make it an advertisement for food, let alone for food high in fat, salt, or sugar.

The opening phrase "really buttery" does not change the analysis. In context, it is part of the creator’s spoken style and is not used to identify, describe, or sell a food product. In plain words, it is stray language, not food marketing.

The instruction also says not to consider destination-page issues or out-of-scope materials. Even without looking beyond the content itself, the promoted category is plainly men’s grooming. So the correct conclusion on these facts is that the content does not clearly market HFSS food.
